payload.subject: hot orch-state row and cold backlog-detail map disagree on next_agent; effective_next_agent() prefers cold, silently misrouting rows
payload.mechanism: effective_next_agent($detail_items) returns $detail_items[.id].next_agent whenever it is a non-empty string, and falls back to the hot rows .next_agent only when that is absent. Nothing reconciles the two, and nothing warns when they disagree.

live_instances.consequence: PRIMARY QA-drain predicate effective_next_agent == qa evaluates FALSE, so the row is invisible to the qa lane its own closeout routed it to. It was NOT picked this tick despite qa[]=3 against QA_CAP=10 and 5 budget remaining. It instead falls into the SECONDARY owner-triage set, whose resolver targets developer, which would re-spawn a developer on already-finished work.

SECONDARY-drain dispatched dev-mcp-server this tick per the cold value. Correct by the resolvers stated design, but a human or any picker reading the hot row would expect architect. Divergence passed explicitly to the spawned agent rather than hidden.

payload.why_this_is_systemic: Both instances arose from agents cold-storing narrative into docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json as part of their own closeout, while writing a different next_agent on the hot row in the same cycle. The 12000B prose ceiling actively pushes agents toward cold-storing, so the write pattern that produces this divergence is the one the system rewards. Two independent instances in a single tick.
asks: Decide the SSOT: should effective_next_agent prefer hot or cold, or refuse to resolve and escalate when they disagree?
Add a divergence detector so a hot/cold next_agent mismatch is visible rather than silently deciding routing.
FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-SCORES-DELIBERATELY-DISABLED-LAUNCHD-JOB-AS-DEGRADED needs its cold next_agent corrected to qa, or it will not reach QA on any future tick.
payload.router_note: Router does not author task rows. Filed as a signal for architect triage.
